external_entities.name: insurance partner
external_entities.description: One of three insurance partners that provides a daily extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Three insurance partners drop a daily extract for us.
external_entities.notes: Represents the three insurance partners as one external-entity type.

external_entities.name: analyst
external_entities.description: An analyst who queries the warehouse directly.

processes.name: Airflow scheduler
processes.description: A scheduler that runs at 02:00, lists the landing bucket, reads files, and triggers a Spark transform job for each file.
processes.source_excerpt: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there.

processes.name: Spark transform job
processes.description: A Spark job that normalizes records before loading them into BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket into which the insurance partners push daily extract files containing claim records with member names and dates of birth.
data_stores.source_excerpt: They push files into a landing bucket over SFTP.
data_stores.notes: The source does not state how the landing bucket is encrypted: "I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted". "Both are on defaults as far as I know."

data_stores.name: Airflow metadata database
data_stores.description: Airflow's metadata database, which stores its connection strings and partner keys.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
data_stores.notes: The source does not state whether this database is encrypted at rest: "I don't know ... whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest." "Both are on defaults as far as I know."

data_stores.name: BigQuery
data_stores.description: The warehouse data store containing normalized claim records queried by analysts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

data_flows.name: daily extract
data_flows.description: An insurance partner pushes a daily extract file into the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They push files into a landing bucket over SFTP.
data_flows.data_description: Claim records with member names and dates of birth.

data_flows.name: list and read landing files
data_flows.description: The Airflow scheduler lists the landing bucket and reads files from it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there
data_flows.notes: The scheduler does not check that a file came from the partner whose folder it landed in.
data_flows.data_description: Daily extract files containing claim records.

data_flows.name: connection strings and partner keys
data_flows.description: Airflow keeps connection strings and partner keys in its metadata database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

data_flows.name: trigger Spark transform job
data_flows.description: For each file, the Airflow scheduler triggers a Spark transform job.
data_flows.source_excerpt: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network.

data_flows.name: normalized records
data_flows.description: The Spark transform job loads normalized records into BigQuery.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.
data_flows.notes: Nothing validates the row contents beyond the schema.
data_flows.data_description: Normalized claim records with member names and dates of birth.

data_flows.name: warehouse query
data_flows.description: An analyst queries the warehouse directly using SSO.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Analysts query the warehouse directly. They are on the warehouse network and authenticate with SSO
data_flows.notes: The grant is dataset-wide and member-identifying columns have not been split out.
data_flows.data_description: Warehouse records, including member-identifying claim data.

assumptions.assumption: The insurance partner is in a separate trust zone because it is an external party that controls its own environment.
assumptions.basis: The text identifies three insurance partners as external parties that push files to the system.

assumptions.assumption: The insurance partner zone is tenant-controlled.
assumptions.basis: The insurance partners are separate external organizations from the system operator.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket's contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The bucket contains claim records with member names and dates of birth, which are personal and health-related data.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow metadata database's contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The database stores connection strings and partner keys, which are credentials and secrets.
